alg-haken-jaco-tollefson-unknot-recognit.empty: An empty coordinate subset Z is allowed in the Jaco–Tollefson branch, but an accepted surface must have nonempty essential disk boundary. The zero vector in the Haken box is not accepted merely because it occurs in the finite list.
alg-haken-jaco-tollefson-unknot-recognit.zero: The crossing-free knot still has a positive triangulation bound C(n+1); n=0 does not mean an empty triangulation. Both surface searches reject the zero normal vector as a disk certificate.
alg-haken-jaco-tollefson-unknot-recognit.one: The validated input has one knot component. A one-generator crossing-free presentation and one accepted disk witness are allowed; inputs with multiple components fail the explicit knot-code test.
alg-haken-jaco-tollefson-unknot-recognit.endpoints: Boundary here is the actual torus boundary of the exterior, not an endpoint of a numerical parameter interval. Acceptance tests the normal surface boundary and its meridional intersection before returning a certificate.
alg-haken-jaco-tollefson-unknot-recognit.nonempty-choice: The searches traverse explicitly bounded finite integer vectors or finitely specified primitive rays and their disk tests. No arbitrary selection from an unspecified family of nonempty sets is part of this procedure.
alg-haken-jaco-tollefson-unknot-recognit.degenerate: Invalid planar incidences, nontransverse crossings, incompatible normal quadrilaterals and a zero ray are handled by validation or rejection. These are actual invalid-input/certificate branches, not silently admitted disks.
alg-haken-jaco-tollefson-unknot-recognit.iff-forward: NA: This item defines two finite searches and their acceptance tests; it does not state the forward half of a correctness equivalence between unknotting and arbitrary search output.
alg-haken-jaco-tollefson-unknot-recognit.iff-reverse: NA: The procedure Definition does not claim that every unknot yields an accepted witness within these bounds. Completeness of either search is not an unstated converse of its acceptance rule.

cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-.empty: The extremal profile is normalized to a positive finite u and its squared weights have nonzero total. An empty active profile cannot meet these hypotheses; no empty-alternative Gaussian limit is asserted.
cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-.zero: NA: The sharp asymptotic assumes u stays in a compact subset of (0,infinity). The exact zero-signal profile and the regime u→0 are not cases of this particular sharp-limit statement.
cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-.one: A single normalized nonzero weight cannot satisfy max_j|w_j|→0. Thus the sharp central-limit conclusion is not asserted for a one-coordinate alternative merely by substituting its weight.
cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-.endpoints: The risk level is alpha in (0,1), not alpha=0 or1. The proof uses a left quantile and strict upper-tail rejection, which preserves the claimed level even when a finite-sample distribution has atoms.
cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-.nonempty-choice: Countable Choice is explicitly assumed for the statistical interfaces. The extremal profile and its positive normalization are hypotheses; the proof does not select profiles from an unproved nonempty optimizer set.
cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-.degenerate: The vanishing maximal-weight condition and positive bounded u exclude a dominant-coordinate or zero-normalizer degeneration. The stated uniform approximation uses precisely those hypotheses.
cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-.iff-forward: NA: The claim gives sharp asymptotic testing risks under an extremal-profile and small-maximal-weight regime, rather than an if-and-only-if characterization of all profile sequences.
cor-ip-ellipsoid-sharp-gaussian-testing-.iff-reverse: NA: No converse says that observing this risk limit forces the displayed profile or maximal-weight hypotheses. Those are sufficient hypotheses for the proved asymptotics.

def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-.empty: The empty framed link is permitted: its ribbon diagram evaluates to the identity of the tensor unit. It is not a zero morphism merely because there are no colored components.
def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-.zero: A framing is nowhere zero; a zero normal vector field is not allowed framing data. A zero morphism in the category may evaluate a diagram to zero without making the construction undefined.
def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-.one: One colored component and the tensor-unit color are legitimate inputs. The evaluation lands in End(1); it need not be identified with the coefficient field unless that additional category hypothesis is given.
def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-.endpoints: The input is a closed framed link, so there are no free tangle endpoints requiring additional boundary objects. The framed Reidemeister conventions retain twists rather than erasing a framing at a diagram boundary.
def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-.nonempty-choice: Colors and their specified dual/ribbon data are supplied on finitely many components. The stated Countable Choice interface for the evaluator is retained; it is not replaced by an unsupported choice-free existence claim.
def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-.degenerate: Singular diagrams and vanishing framing fields are outside the framed-link input. Crossings and extrema are represented by the specified braiding and duality morphisms, including their identity cases.
def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-.iff-forward: NA: This Definition specifies evaluation from supplied ribbon-category data; it does not characterize which arbitrary link functions arise from such a category.
def-colored-framed-knot-evaluation-from-.iff-reverse: NA: No inverse reconstruction of a ribbon category from evaluated colored links is claimed. The invariance/evaluation conventions are not a biconditional classification.

def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi.empty: A finite family of zero disks imposes no pairwise or dual-sphere equations; those conditions are vacuous. The ambient connected based manifold is nevertheless nonempty, so empty disk data are not an empty ambient example.
def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi.zero: The relative normal Euler obstruction may be zero; this is exactly the extension condition for the supplied boundary framing. Group-ring intersection zero is distinct from the identity coefficient1 required for a geometric dual.
def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi.one: For one disk, the duality equation is lambda(f_1,g_1)=1, not0. With no distinct disks the off-diagonal equations are vacuous, but the self-intersection and framing conditions remain.
def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi.endpoints: The disk boundary framing is prescribed on its boundary collar and the relative Euler obstruction tests extension across the whole disk. Proper disk boundary and interior transverse double points have different local models.
def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi.nonempty-choice: The disks, spheres, whiskers and framings are part of a finite supplied datum. The Definition of a good group does not itself construct such a datum for every arbitrary manifold.
def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi.degenerate: The specified immersed-disk models allow transverse double points with algebraically controlled intersections, not arbitrary triple points or tangent singularities. A failed framing obstruction is not silently treated as framed.
def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi.iff-forward: The Definition says the relative Euler obstruction vanishes precisely when the fixed boundary normal framing extends. In the forward direction, zero obstruction is the defining obstruction-theoretic criterion for extension; it is not the disk-embedding theorem.
def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi.iff-reverse: An extension of the given boundary framing has zero relative normal Euler obstruction by its defining obstruction construction. This is the actual local iff in the Definition, distinct from any characterization of good groups.

def-knot-a-polynomial.empty: The abelian peripheral curve L=1 is retained, so the reduced one-dimensional locus is not empty for this knot definition. Zero-dimensional nonabelian components are deliberately not factors of the A-polynomial.
def-knot-a-polynomial.zero: M and L belong to C*, so zero eigenvalues are excluded. The defining polynomial is a nonzero reduced generator, not the zero polynomial, and isolated image points are omitted from its curve factor.
def-knot-a-polynomial.one: The abelian factor L−1 is present; thus the unit polynomial1 is not the ordinary A-polynomial under this convention. A single abelian curve is a legitimate remaining locus.
def-knot-a-polynomial.endpoints: The peripheral torus supplies the ordered meridian and preferred longitude. These are marking data, not limits M=0 or L=0: both variables remain invertible Laurent variables.
def-knot-a-polynomial.nonempty-choice: The A-polynomial Definition assumes AC for its algebraic-geometry framework and fixes peripheral markings. No canonical representative is chosen from polynomial units without the stated primitive/normalization convention.
def-knot-a-polynomial.degenerate: Repeated curve components are reduced and zero-dimensional images are discarded. This is why reducible representations or a lower-dimensional image are not counted with artificial multiplicity.
def-knot-a-polynomial.iff-forward: The Definition explicitly equates retaining the abelian curve with divisibility by L−1 in the Laurent representative. A polynomial vanishing on every (M,1) has zero remainder on division by L−1.
def-knot-a-polynomial.iff-reverse: Conversely an L−1 factor makes the representative vanish on the abelian peripheral curve. This equivalence concerns the retained factor, not a characterization of which Laurent polynomials are realized by knots.

def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space.empty: The empty closed oriented manifold is the zero bordism representative. Allowing it does not make X empty: X is assumed path connected with its CW-space convention.
def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space.zero: Zero is represented by the empty manifold with its unique map to X. A nullbordism has boundary M and its map restricts to f; it is not obtained by setting the target map to a numeric zero.
def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space.one: The one-point target is allowed and recovers ordinary oriented bordism. A single connected source component is allowed, while disconnected representatives and disjoint-union addition are retained.
def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space.endpoints: The bordism boundary is identified with M_0 disjoint union minus M_1, and the target map must restrict to the two given maps. Boundary orientation is part of the relation, not an optional endpoint sign.
def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space.nonempty-choice: The datum consists of one finite-dimensional manifold and one map; an asserted bordism includes its actual manifold, boundary identification and map. No indexed family of choices of representatives is made.
def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space.degenerate: Disconnected and empty representatives are permitted; singular spaces are not substituted for the required closed smooth oriented source manifolds. Product bordisms supply reflexivity even for empty sources.
def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space.iff-forward: NA: The item defines the bordism relation by existence of a marked bordism. It does not claim a separate forward characterization in terms of homology or homotopy invariants.
def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space.iff-reverse: NA: No homological condition is claimed sufficient for a bordism. The existence-of-W criterion is the defining relation, rather than an unproved converse classification theorem.

def-smooth-zero-trace.empty: The attaching knot is an embedded circle and is not empty. The construction attaches one actual two-handle; the empty handle list would give B4 and is not the zero-trace input.
def-smooth-zero-trace.zero: Zero denotes the framing relative to the preferred longitude, not omission of the two-handle or a zero-dimensional attaching region. The boundary is the corresponding zero surgery.
def-smooth-zero-trace.one: Exactly one two-handle is attached to B4 along the given knot. No multi-component link or one-dimensional handle is implicit in this trace Definition.
def-smooth-zero-trace.endpoints: The attaching collar lies in the boundary S3 and the remaining handle boundary becomes the surgery boundary after rounding corners. The framing identifies the longitude and hence the actual filled boundary.
def-smooth-zero-trace.nonempty-choice: The knot and zero-framing convention determine the finite attachment datum up to the specified equivalence. No family of arbitrary framings is selected; the chosen tubular identification is part of a representative construction.
def-smooth-zero-trace.degenerate: A singular attaching circle or a nonintegral unspecified framing is not accepted as a smooth handle attachment. Zero framing itself is regular, not a degenerate attachment.
def-smooth-zero-trace.iff-forward: NA: Defining the trace and identifying its boundary surgery does not assert that a boundary homeomorphism forces the original attaching knots to agree.
def-smooth-zero-trace.iff-reverse: NA: No converse recovering K from an arbitrary four-manifold with zero-surgery boundary is claimed. The item only specifies the trace associated to the given K.

ex-ip-sobolev-minimax-rates.empty: The sequence model has infinitely many positive-mode coordinates; Q>0 and the Sobolev class are prescribed. It is not a minimax problem over an empty truth class or an empty frequency set.
ex-ip-sobolev-minimax-rates.zero: The rates are as epsilon decreases through positive values. Substituting epsilon=0 into the logarithmic severe-ill-posed formula is not part of the claim, and Q=0 is excluded by the positive-radius hypothesis.
ex-ip-sobolev-minimax-rates.one: A single retained coefficient is not the infinite Sobolev minimax class. The dimension-dependent powers and exponential singular values are asserted for the full positive-index sequence model.
ex-ip-sobolev-minimax-rates.endpoints: The severely ill-posed expression uses log(1/epsilon) for sufficiently small positive epsilon. The positive regularity and ill-posedness parameter restrictions are retained; no critical endpoint rate is inferred by continuity.
ex-ip-sobolev-minimax-rates.nonempty-choice: Countable Choice is explicitly retained for the Gaussian sequence/minimax framework. The supplied singular system and positive class radius are not selected from an unproved existence assertion.
ex-ip-sobolev-minimax-rates.degenerate: The displayed singular values are positive in the relevant modes. A zero singular value with an undetectable coefficient would violate this model rather than satisfy the same minimax calculation.
ex-ip-sobolev-minimax-rates.iff-forward: NA: The examples calculate rates for specified singular-value sequences; they do not assert that only these operators can realize those rates.
ex-ip-sobolev-minimax-rates.iff-reverse: NA: A rate of this size is not claimed to imply polynomial or exponential singular-value asymptotics. The calculations use the displayed model as input.

lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi.empty: For g=0 the Seifert matrix is empty and already the terminal matrix; its Alexander determinant is1. No nonempty primitive-kernel vector is demanded in this branch.
lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi.zero: For positive genus, the unit Alexander polynomial forces det(V)=0 in the kernel-reduction step; zero determinant is the mechanism for lowering genus, not a forbidden nonsingular-matrix assumption.
lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi.one: Alexander polynomial1 means the unit class under the stated normalization. A one-handle Seifert form can be reduced by the same primitive-kernel construction; it is not a one-by-one Seifert matrix.
lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi.endpoints: The finite reduction stops at genus0, where no further kernel or band is selected. Genus is a nonnegative integer, not an interval parameter with an omitted boundary limit.
lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi.nonempty-choice: The positive-genus kernel step uses a primitive integer vector and finite integral basis operations under the stated AC framework. The g=0 branch makes no such selection.
lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi.degenerate: The proof deliberately permits a singular Seifert matrix while requiring the skew-symmetric intersection form to be unimodular. Conflating those two determinants would remove the very reduction case used.
lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi.iff-forward: NA: This item proves Alexander-one implies S-equivalent to the empty form. It does not state the reverse as a separate characterization of arbitrary matrices beyond its Seifert hypotheses.
lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi.iff-reverse: NA: No conclusion that every algebraically slice Seifert form has Alexander polynomial1 is asserted. S-equivalence to the empty form is the output of the stronger unit-polynomial input.

lem-casson-gordon-bordism-independence-a.empty: Empty added closed bordism components contribute zero; the marked surgery/branched-cover boundary is still a nonempty input. The proof compares actual bounding multiples, not an empty boundary substituted for the knot data.
lem-casson-gordon-bordism-independence-a.zero: A constant character is admitted and its untwisted signature comparison is handled in1.1. At poles the signature is defined using the image/reduced nonsingular form rather than inverting a singular raw matrix.
lem-casson-gordon-bordism-independence-a.one: A single bounding copy r=1 may be used when it exists. In general r must be a positive bounding multiple, so no division by a zero number of copies occurs.
lem-casson-gordon-bordism-independence-a.endpoints: The signature limit in5.1 is theta→0 from the positive side, chosen away from the finite exceptional set. It does not substitute a pole into a nonsingular form or identify two undefined endpoint signatures.
lem-casson-gordon-bordism-independence-a.nonempty-choice: The AC assumption and actual finite bordism/character extensions are retained. A character is not assumed surjective onto an artificially fixed cyclic target;4.1 passes to its actual finite image.
lem-casson-gordon-bordism-independence-a.degenerate: The raw middle-dimensional intersection pairing may have a radical. Step3.1 passes to the appropriate image form before using nonsingularity, so zero or degenerate summands are not silently inverted.
lem-casson-gordon-bordism-independence-a.iff-forward: NA: Independence of the resulting Witt/signature invariant is not a criterion characterizing which characters extend over every bounding manifold.
lem-casson-gordon-bordism-independence-a.iff-reverse: NA: The invariant comparison does not claim that equal signatures imply bordism equivalence. Only invariance and nonsingularity after the specified reduction are proved.

lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c.empty: The projection graph is connected and nonempty in the hypothesis. An empty projection is not an extra graph with two colorings; the proof fixes a complementary region of the actual diagram.
lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c.zero: A crossing-free circle is the familiar two-region coloring when represented as a regular diagram; no crossing sign is needed. In the finite graph argument the even-intersection parity, not a positive crossing count, controls consistency.
lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c.one: A single crossing and graph loops do not obstruct parity coloring. The path-independence argument counts crossings modulo2 rather than assuming distinct edges or at least two crossings.
lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c.endpoints: Paths used for coloring have endpoints in complementary regions and cross projection edges transversely. Endpoints on the graph or a crossing vertex are avoided by the prescribed local path perturbation.
lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c.nonempty-choice: Choosing one region fixes which of the two colors it receives; finitely many region adjacencies then determine the rest. Connectedness of the dual adjacency graph gives exactly two choices, not an arbitrary coloring family.
lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c.degenerate: Repeated edges and loops are accommodated by parity. Nonregular tangencies or non-4-valent crossings are not input regular-link diagrams and are not justified by the coloring proof.
lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c.iff-forward: NA: The theorem asserts existence and uniqueness up to color exchange for a connected regular projection; it does not characterize all embedded graphs admitting a checkerboard coloring.
lem-connected-regular-link-diagram-has-c.iff-reverse: NA: A graph having a checkerboard coloring is not claimed to arise from the stipulated connected regular knot/link projection. That converse is not used.

lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude.empty: An essential properly embedded disk has an actual nonempty boundary circle on the exterior torus. Neither an empty surface nor a closed disk away from that boundary meets the premise.
lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude.zero: The boundary homology class lies in the longitude kernel, but essentiality excludes its being the zero primitive torus class. Consequently the coefficient k of the longitude is ±1 rather than0.
lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude.one: One actual essential disk suffices. Primitivity of its simple essential boundary curve forces longitude multiplicity1 in absolute value; the proof does not assume a family of parallel disks.
lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude.endpoints: Properness places the disk boundary on the exterior torus and its interior off that torus. The longitude conclusion concerns this boundary marking, not an arbitrary interior loop.
lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude.nonempty-choice: The disk is supplied by the hypothesis. Its finite homology calculation and a meridian representative require no selection from all possible essential disks.
lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude.degenerate: A boundary circle that is inessential in the torus would have class0 and is explicitly excluded. The proof uses that exclusion before concluding that its longitudinal multiple is primitive.
lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude.iff-forward: NA: The assertion is that an essential disk boundary has longitude slope. It does not say that every longitude curve on every knot exterior bounds a disk.
lem-essential-disk-boundary-is-longitude.iff-reverse: NA: Longitudinal homology alone is not claimed sufficient for an essential disk. In particular no unknot conclusion is obtained merely from the existence of the longitude marking.

lem-haken-search-acceptance-is-an-essent.empty: The accepted candidate has nonempty boundary and disk Euler characteristic. The empty normal surface cannot meet the acceptance tests, even though zero coordinates belong to the ambient bounded enumeration.
lem-haken-search-acceptance-is-an-essent.zero: The zero normal vector fails the nonempty disk-boundary test. Odd meridional intersection of an accepted candidate is also nonzero and is used to establish essentiality.
lem-haken-search-acceptance-is-an-essent.one: The conclusion applies to one accepted Haken candidate, including a disk with a single boundary component. It makes no claim that multiple accepted disks must agree.
lem-haken-search-acceptance-is-an-essent.endpoints: The candidate boundary lies in the exterior boundary torus. Its odd meridian intersection excludes a nullhomologous boundary there, giving the essential-boundary condition actually required.
lem-haken-search-acceptance-is-an-essent.nonempty-choice: The acceptance witness is already given by the algorithm premise. The proof need not choose an accepted candidate from an unexplored infinite surface class.
lem-haken-search-acceptance-is-an-essent.degenerate: Matching and quadrilateral constraints are checked before disk acceptance. An incompatible normal vector or a closed sphere of Euler characteristic2 does not pass the disk tests.
lem-haken-search-acceptance-is-an-essent.iff-forward: NA: This lemma proves soundness of the Haken acceptance branch. It does not prove the converse search-completeness assertion or soundness of an unrelated Jaco–Tollefson branch.
lem-haken-search-acceptance-is-an-essent.iff-reverse: NA: Existence of an essential disk is not here shown to force this finite search to accept. Only an already accepted normal vector is interpreted geometrically.

lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-.empty: The inherited separation radius r is positive and v belongs to the separated alternative, so its finite active support J cannot be empty. Formally the empty likelihood product would be1 and u=0, but that is not an admissible separated profile.
lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-.zero: Zero individual v_j entries contribute cosh(0)=1 and do not invalidate the finite product bound. The all-zero profile is excluded by v in Theta_q(r) with r>0; epsilon remains positive.
lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-.one: For one active coordinate the Rademacher mixture has the displayed single cosh likelihood and the second-moment estimate remains valid. No central-limit small-maximal-weight condition is needed here.
lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-.endpoints: The testing risk convention fixes alpha in (0,1) and epsilon>0. No division by zero noise or endpoint normal quantile is made in the mixture inequality.
lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-.nonempty-choice: Only finitely many independent signs are mixed on the given finite J; Countable Choice is retained for the surrounding Gaussian sequence model. The argument does not need to choose a new extremal alternative.
lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-.degenerate: Some coordinates of v may vanish; their likelihood factors are1. The finite nonzero fourth-moment normalization is controlled by the separated-profile premise, not by an assumption that every listed coordinate is nonzero.
lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-.iff-forward: NA: The second-moment computation supplies lower bounds on testing risk from a given mixture; it does not characterize every experiment with the same risk.
lem-ip-gaussian-product-mixture-testing-.iff-reverse: NA: A small testing risk is not claimed to imply failure of this mixture construction. These are sufficient mixture lower-bound estimates, not a converse criterion.

lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined.empty: Each input knot is a nonempty oriented circle; a zero-crossing unknot is allowed. An empty link is not one of the two summands, so deleting a summand is not a hidden empty-input operation.
lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined.zero: Zero crossings cause no problem because the construction removes a standard local arc, not a crossing. The chart rescaling includes its derivative-limit value at scale0 as specified in1.2.
lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined.one: The operation takes two knots; if one is an unknot its local arc and collar still exist. It is not defined by choosing one special crossing or requiring a nontrivial knot.
lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined.endpoints: The removed arc endpoints are matched with the specified oriented standard collars. Transition maps must respect that orientation; an orientation-reversing arbitrary gluing is not an equivalent marked connected sum.
lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined.nonempty-choice: Countable Choice is retained for the stated isotopy interfaces. The proof uses finitely many supplied chart/arc choices and compares them by the actual compact isotopy-extension argument.
lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined.degenerate: A small standard ball has positive radius and a genuine embedded arc. Singular arcs or a chart transition reversing the required orientation are not admitted choices in the well-definedness statement.
lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined.iff-forward: NA: Well-definedness says changing permitted construction choices preserves the resulting knot class; it does not classify all decompositions of a knot into prime summands.
lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined.iff-reverse: NA: Equal connected-sum results are not asserted to imply equal summands or identical gluing data. Cancellation and prime decomposition are not conclusions of this lemma.

lem-l2-cellular-duality-and-weak-exactne.empty: Finite cellular chain blocks may have rank0 and give zero Hilbert modules; cap duality and weak exactness then have their zero-space interpretation. The actual compact manifold/group datum is not replaced by missing chain complexes.
lem-l2-cellular-duality-and-weak-exactne.zero: Zero reduced homology and zero projections are allowed. Kernels and closures of images, rather than an inverse of a zero or nonclosed map, define the reduced Hilbert statements.
lem-l2-cellular-duality-and-weak-exactne.one: The trivial group and rank-one free cellular blocks are permitted. Their von Neumann-module reductions specialize to the ordinary Hilbert/cellular calculation without a nontrivial-group hypothesis.
lem-l2-cellular-duality-and-weak-exactne.endpoints: For manifold pairs, the boundary and relative chain blocks use the displayed cap-product conventions. Weak exactness means equality after taking the specified closures, not surjectivity at an omitted endpoint term.
lem-l2-cellular-duality-and-weak-exactne.nonempty-choice: The Statement explicitly assumes AC for its Hilbert-module framework. Finite CW structures and actual chain maps are inputs; no choice-free strengthening is inferred from finite cell counts.
lem-l2-cellular-duality-and-weak-exactne.degenerate: A nonclosed operator range is handled by its closure, and pairing radicals are removed before duality. An algebraically exact sequence is not silently promoted to a sequence of closed-range isomorphisms.
lem-l2-cellular-duality-and-weak-exactne.iff-forward: NA: The asserted dualities and weak exactness are properties of the supplied cellular L2 construction, not an iff test for whether a manifold has a given group.
lem-l2-cellular-duality-and-weak-exactne.iff-reverse: NA: Vanishing L2 homology is not claimed to determine the underlying topology or imply the geometric hypotheses. Only the stated analytic/cellular consequences are used.

lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i.empty: The surface is connected and has its nonempty longitudinal boundary in the knot exterior. The empty surface cannot satisfy these hypotheses or serve as a fiber representative.
lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i.zero: Genus0 is included: the disk-fiber case is handled in3.1 instead of invoking positive-genus surface-group arguments. No nonzero rank is required of the disk fundamental group.
lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i.one: One connected nonseparating incompressible longitudinal surface is the input. The theorem does not require several parallel fibers or two independent boundary components.
lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i.endpoints: The proper boundary curves have the specified longitude marking; the isotopy to a fiber respects the aligned boundary convention. There is no free choice of a different peripheral slope at the boundary.
lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i.nonempty-choice: The fibered exterior, surface and markings are supplied under the stated AC assumption. The proof compares this surface with an existing fiber; it does not select a fibration from all knot exteriors.
lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i.degenerate: Separating or compressible surfaces are excluded, because the covering/surface-group argument uses nonseparation and incompressibility. The disk fiber is a genuine included case rather than such a degeneration.
lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i.iff-forward: NA: In a given fibered exterior the stated longitudinal incompressible surface is identified with a fiber. No converse says existence of any longitudinal surface alone makes the knot fibered.
lem-nonseparating-longitudinal-surface-i.iff-reverse: NA: The theorem does not classify nonfibered exteriors by failure of a particular surface isotopy. Fiberedness is a hypothesis throughout.

lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4.empty: The conic is an actual nonempty embedded S2 with a disk-bundle neighborhood. Its complement is not obtained by removing an empty set from the ambient manifold.
lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4.zero: Positive-degree rational homology vanishes, while H0 is Q. The integral Z/2 phenomenon is retained, so rational-ball terminology does not assert integral acyclicity.
lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4.one: There is one connected boundary lens space L(4,1) with the stated orientation convention. It is not the trivial lens space S3 obtained by replacing4 with1.
lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4.endpoints: The normal circle bundle has Euler number4, computed from the actual transition function. The induced boundary orientation is tracked; the result is not an orientation-free equality of surgery coefficients.
lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4.nonempty-choice: The AC framework and explicit conic/tubular-neighborhood data are retained. A rational homology computation does not choose or assert an arbitrary filling for every lens space.
lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4.degenerate: The conic is nonsingular and its normal Euler number is4 rather than0. A reducible or singular conic would not give the embedded sphere used in the disk-bundle construction.
lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4.iff-forward: NA: This constructs one rational ball with the displayed lens-space boundary, not a classification of which lens spaces bound rational balls.
lem-rational-ball-b2-bounds-lens-l4.iff-reverse: NA: A rational filling of some lens space is not claimed to force the conic construction or the same integral homology. No such converse is used.

lem-slice-branched-cover-produces-defini.empty: The branching disk and its boundary knot are nonempty, and the cover has its given boundary M. Empty branching would be a different unbranched construction and is not covered.
lem-slice-branched-cover-produces-defini.zero: Rank-zero b2 is allowed: positive definiteness of the zero intersection form is vacuous, and Mayer–Vietoris still gives the displayed b2 formula. The proof never divides by that rank.
lem-slice-branched-cover-produces-defini.one: The construction is a double branched cover with one marked rational-homology-sphere gluing boundary, not a variable number of sheets. A single supplied positive-definite filling is enough.
lem-slice-branched-cover-produces-defini.endpoints: The cover piece is glued with reversed boundary orientation along M using actual collars. This boundary marking is what permits the homology and normal-generation pi1 arguments.
lem-slice-branched-cover-produces-defini.nonempty-choice: The AC assumption and given smooth filling/branching data are retained. The theorem constructs from those data and does not assert existence of a positive-definite filling for every cover.
lem-slice-branched-cover-produces-defini.degenerate: The rational-homology-sphere and normal-generation conditions are essential: the proof uses them to remove extra middle homology and the fundamental group. They are not dropped in a degenerate boundary case.
lem-slice-branched-cover-produces-defini.iff-forward: NA: The claim constructs a definite closed four-manifold from supplied slicing and filling data; it does not characterize all definite four-manifolds as such gluings.
lem-slice-branched-cover-produces-defini.iff-reverse: NA: Existence of the resulting definite form is not asserted sufficient for sliceness. The logical direction is the obstruction-producing construction from a slice disk.

lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid.empty: The normalized complex has a specified nonzero total homology generator, so the admissible cycle family used to define tau is not empty. A zero complex is not an admitted marked knot complex.
lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid.zero: Setting extra basepoint variables to zero is performed on polynomial chain maps and homotopies. This is a literal specialization identity, not an unjustified assertion that every quotient is flat.
lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid.one: A singly pointed-pair knot has no extra V factor; its distinguished factor is the unit. The comparison does not manufacture an extra exterior-generator summand in this case.
lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid.endpoints: The filtration origin is fixed by the marked Seifert normalization on both diagrams. Equality of relative filtrations without that origin would not determine the same integer tau.
lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid.nonempty-choice: Countable Choice and the supplied finite pointed move comparisons are retained. The total-generator normalization rules out choosing an arbitrary nonzero class in an unspecified homology group.
lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid.degenerate: Extra acyclic terms are harmless only through the stated filtered homotopies; an empty total generator or an arbitrary multipointed factor is not normalized by fiat.
lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid.iff-forward: NA: The theorem proves diagram independence of a normalized integer, not a characterization of knots having a specified tau value.
lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid.iff-reverse: NA: Equal tau values are not claimed to imply equivalence of Heegaard diagrams, knots or filtered complexes. The assertion only compares diagrams of the same marked knot.

thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top.empty: At genus0 the Seifert matrix and compression list are empty, and the existing Seifert disk is the required disk. The knot itself remains a nonempty circle.
thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top.zero: Zero genus is handled separately in1.1. The Alexander hypothesis is the unit polynomial1, not a zero polynomial or a vanishing determinant interpreted as that polynomial.
thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top.one: A single Seifert handle is permitted and enters the same finite reduction. Polynomial1 is a unit class; it does not mean the degree-one polynomial t−1.
thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top.endpoints: The construction retains the actual boundary knot collar and its normal framing. The resulting disk is locally flat topological; smoothness is not inferred at the boundary from the topological disk theorem.
thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top.nonempty-choice: The Statement explicitly assumes full AC for the imported topological disk machinery. No Countable-Choice-only or choice-free strengthening is made by this boundary disposition.
thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top.degenerate: Empty handle data at genus0 are legitimate. In positive genus the unimodular Seifert-intersection conditions are preserved; an arbitrary singular surface is not admitted as a Seifert disk.
thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top.iff-forward: NA: The theorem gives the sufficient condition Delta=1 for topological sliceness. It does not state that every topologically slice knot has trivial Alexander polynomial.
thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top.iff-reverse: NA: The reverse implication topologically slice⇒Alexander polynomial1 is not asserted. The one-way disk construction must not be upgraded to that false classification.

thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-.empty: The claim ranges over actual Newton edges of the retained curve polynomial. A zero-length vector or an omitted zero-dimensional representation component is not an edge to which a slope is assigned.
thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-.zero: The edge normal is a nonzero integral vector, defined up to sign. A zero valuation pair would not define its boundary slope and is not used as a primitive edge normal.
thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-.one: One actual edge is enough to obtain the associated essential surface. No minimum number of nonabelian factors or two independent edge directions is assumed.
thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-.endpoints: Vertical edge data are allowed and correspond to the infinite slope convention rather than division by zero. The boundary slope is a peripheral class, not an endpoint value of a real interval.
thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-.nonempty-choice: Full AC and the supplied algebraic-curve/ideal-point framework are explicit. The finite extension/valuation choices are made for the chosen edge, not asserted to be canonical for every polynomial.
thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-.degenerate: Reducible representations and isolated image points are treated by the ordinary reduced A-polynomial convention. The proof does not assume a generic smooth point represents every exceptional boundary value.
thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-.iff-forward: NA: Every Newton edge slope is shown to be a boundary slope; not every boundary slope is claimed to occur on the ordinary A-polynomial Newton polygon.
thm-ccgls-newton-edge-slope-is-boundary-.iff-reverse: NA: No converse realizes an arbitrary essential-surface boundary slope as a Newton edge. The edge-to-surface construction is the stated direction.

thm-explicit-mitoses-give-functorial-int.empty: The trivial input group is allowed, but its mitosis still includes the specified stable letters. An empty bar-chain support is filled by zero; it is not a missing nonempty generator choice.
thm-explicit-mitoses-give-functorial-int.zero: Acyclicity here is vanishing in positive degrees; H0 remains Z. The construction does not call a nonempty connected classifying space reduced-acyclic by setting its ordinary H0 to zero.
thm-explicit-mitoses-give-functorial-int.one: The identity group and degree-one cycles are included in the formulas. Group identity labels are multiplicative1, distinct from the zero chain; normalized degenerate simplices are handled before claiming a filling.
thm-explicit-mitoses-give-functorial-int.endpoints: The construction uses the discrete stages G→m(G)→… and their union, with explicit transition embeddings. It is not a continuous parameter family requiring a limit-time homeomorphism.
thm-explicit-mitoses-give-functorial-int.nonempty-choice: Full AC is stated. Each individual bar cycle has finite support and the proof gives finite fillings at a sufficiently advanced stage; it does not invoke an unspecified simultaneous choice of all fillings.
thm-explicit-mitoses-give-functorial-int.degenerate: Identity-labelled degenerate bar simplices are included in the normalization discussion. Their treatment is necessary to distinguish a normalized zero chain from an unaccounted nonzero boundary.
thm-explicit-mitoses-give-functorial-int.iff-forward: NA: The functorial construction embeds each group into an acyclic envelope; it does not characterize which groups were already acyclic.
thm-explicit-mitoses-give-functorial-int.iff-reverse: NA: Acyclicity of the envelope is not claimed to imply acyclicity of its subgroup. Naturality and injectivity of the construction do not give that converse.

thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo.empty: The group extension has its identity elements and connected classifying spaces, so there is no empty base or fiber. Empty higher-degree chain groups can still yield zero entries on a spectral-sequence diagonal.
thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo.zero: The p=0 and q=0 edges belong to the first quadrant; H0 of the identity group is Z rather than0. At total degree0 only E2_(0,0) contributes.
thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo.one: Either N=1 or Q=1 is allowed and gives the corresponding trivial-extension specialization. The usual identity coefficients and collapsed positive-degree homology are retained.
thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo.endpoints: Exactness at the two identity-group ends of 1→N→G→Q→1 is part of the input extension. The filtration of H_n has its actual finite first and last terms, not an omitted convergence endpoint.
thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo.nonempty-choice: Full AC is explicitly part of the stated group-homology framework. The extension maps and module actions are given data; a section is not assumed to be a homomorphism or chosen without its stated framework.
thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo.degenerate: Trivial kernels or quotients are legitimate. Surjectivity of G→Q and identification of N with its kernel are retained; a nonexact sequence is not treated as a degenerate extension.
thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo.iff-forward: NA: An exact group extension produces the spectral sequence. The theorem does not characterize all spectral sequences as arising from extensions.
thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo.iff-reverse: NA: Existence of groups with the displayed E2 terms does not assert an extension realizing them. No converse extension construction follows from convergence alone.

thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-com.empty: The knots are nonempty circles. The empty product convention of a monoid, when used, is the unknot identity, not an empty embedded link.
thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-com.zero: A crossing-free unknot represents the identity class, not a zero knot with empty underlying set. The identity gluing uses its actual standard arc and ball.
thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-com.one: The two-sided unit proof covers K#unknot and unknot#K. Thus a product with one nonunit factor retains that knot class.
thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-com.endpoints: The standard arc collars and their oriented endpoint pairings are retained under the half-turn and associativity isotopies. No interval-endpoint limit is used to exchange factors.
thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-com.nonempty-choice: The stated Countable Choice interfaces for knot isotopy and connected-sum well-definedness are retained. A finite product is handled by finite composition, not arbitrary representatives of every knot class.
thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-com.degenerate: The unknot is included and gives the unit; singular knots and empty links are outside the smooth oriented knot domain. No inverse knot is asserted in this monoid theorem.
thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-com.iff-forward: NA: The result establishes the monoid laws, not a criterion that detects whether two arbitrary connected-sum decompositions are equal.
thm-oriented-knot-connected-sum-is-a-com.iff-reverse: NA: Commutativity and associativity do not assert cancellation, inverses or prime uniqueness. Those converse/cancellation claims are absent.

thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and.empty: For a crossing-free knot the crossing list is empty, but there is one Seifert circle and one disk. The surface is not empty and its genus formula gives0.
thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and.zero: c=0 and connected one-knot boundary force s=1 in this construction, so g=(0−1+1)/2=0. The formula is not applied to an arbitrary empty link with s=0.
thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and.one: One crossing is allowed. For example c=1,s=2 gives genus0; the one-boundary orientable-surface condition prevents treating c=1,s=1 as an admissible half-integral genus case.
thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and.endpoints: The boundary is exactly the oriented input knot after band attachment and rounding. Its being one component is essential in converting Euler characteristic to 1−2g.
thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and.nonempty-choice: The finite oriented diagram supplies its Seifert circles and crossing bands under the stated Countable Choice framework. No global choice of a minimal-genus surface is required.
thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and.degenerate: Repeated visits to a Seifert circle are permitted, but the final surface is connected with one boundary component. Only pairs (s,c) realized by that construction enter the integer genus formula.
thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and.iff-forward: NA: The formula computes the genus of the constructed Seifert surface and hence an upper bound for knot genus. It does not say that every Seifert surface is genus-minimizing.
thm-seifert-algorithm-boundary-euler-and.iff-reverse: NA: A numerical genus upper bound is not claimed to characterize which diagrams realize a knot or when the Seifert algorithm is optimal.

thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-.empty: The defining infinity homology has the normalized tower generator, so its representing-cycle set is nonempty. The zero complex is not an admitted replacement for the knot complex.
thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-.zero: At t=0 the normalized ordinary tower gives Upsilon0=0. If the four-ball genus is0, the stated bound on [0,1] forces Upsilon to vanish there and symmetry gives vanishing on the remaining half.
thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-.one: The value t=1 lies in the stated closed genus-bound interval. Additivity applies to two knots even when either is the unknot, whose normalized complex supplies the unit.
thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-.endpoints: Reflection t↔2−t and Upsilon(0)=0 give Upsilon(2)=0. The derivative formula uses the right derivative at0; no two-sided derivative or an unproved differentiability at every corner is asserted.
thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-.nonempty-choice: The Countable Choice and exact source-qualified filtered-complex inputs remain explicit. The minimum is taken over representatives of the existing generator, not over an assumed nonempty family for an arbitrary acyclic complex.
thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-.degenerate: Acyclic summands or repeated affine minimizers may produce corners but do not remove the tower class. The genus estimate is used only on its declared t interval, then extended by the stated symmetry.
thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-.iff-forward: NA: Additivity, mirror symmetry and the genus inequality are not a criterion characterizing slice knots by Upsilon=0.
thm-upsilon-additivity-mirror-and-genus-.iff-reverse: NA: Vanishing Upsilon is not asserted sufficient for smooth sliceness. Nor is equality in its genus bound claimed to determine the knot.

ex-ip-analytic-missing-angle-covector.empty: The angle set is nonempty proper open and antipodally invariant, with a nonempty omitted angular arc. The exhibited covector lies in that missing arc, not in an empty acquisition experiment.
ex-ip-analytic-missing-angle-covector.zero: The covector is nonzero and its conormal parameter tau is nonzero. Zero frequency is outside the wavefront/canonical-relation assertion, so it is not used as an invisible singular direction.
ex-ip-analytic-missing-angle-covector.one: One point and one nonzero omitted covector suffice for the counterexample to visibility. No multiple-singularity interference or many-component input is needed.
ex-ip-analytic-missing-angle-covector.endpoints: If a direction lies on the boundary of the open measured angle set, it is not in that set. The canonical-relation condition uses actual membership, not membership only in its closure.
ex-ip-analytic-missing-angle-covector.degenerate: The weight is the constant1 and is nowhere zero, so invisibility here is missing angular coverage rather than a vanishing weight. Nonzero covectors remain part of the hypothesis.
ex-ip-analytic-missing-angle-covector.iff-forward: NA: The example exhibits an invisible covector using the actual measured canonical relation. It does not assert a reconstruction theorem or a full iff criterion for recovering arbitrary singular distributions.
ex-ip-analytic-missing-angle-covector.iff-reverse: NA: Absence of this particular covector from the measured relation is the example conclusion; no converse says all unseen data must have the same missing-angle construction.

ex-knot-kt-21-worked-cases.empty: The knot and its mirrored reversed copy are nonempty. A genus-zero Seifert disk has an empty handle list, but the construction still contains an actual disk and boundary knot.
ex-knot-kt-21-worked-cases.one: The unknot is an allowed choice of K and yields the standard slice connected sum. One arbitrary K also suffices; no nontriviality hypothesis is hidden in the ribbon construction.
ex-knot-kt-21-worked-cases.endpoints: The two punctured boundary collars and oriented band attachments are matched as specified. The disk boundary is K#mirror(reverse K), not a link with unpaired endpoints.
ex-knot-kt-21-worked-cases.degenerate: Genus0 and an empty band list are included. The finite construction produces a disk without maxima rather than assuming every smooth slice disk can be rearranged to be ribbon.
ex-knot-kt-21-worked-cases.nonempty-choice: The Countable Choice convention and the supplied finite diagram/surface data are retained. The example needs one such construction, not a simultaneous family of Seifert surfaces for every knot.
ex-knot-kt-21-worked-cases.iff-forward: NA: This proves K#mirror(reverse K) is ribbon and slice. It does not characterize all ribbon knots as such doubles.
ex-knot-kt-21-worked-cases.iff-reverse: NA: A slice knot is not asserted to admit this doubled form, nor is the slice-ribbon conjecture used. Only the explicit example direction is needed.

lem-ip-distributional-radon-representati.zero: If all test integrals vanish, the signed-measure uniqueness argument forces the measure to be0. This included zero-measure case does not need a nonzero total-variation normalization.
lem-ip-distributional-radon-representati.one: The proof compares two measures by their difference; one zero measure is allowed. The compact-test approximation works without assuming both positive and negative parts are nonzero.
lem-ip-distributional-radon-representati.endpoints: Compact subsets and compactly supported smooth tests remain inside the given open domain. No boundary distribution outside that open set is reconstructed by this uniqueness statement.
lem-ip-distributional-radon-representati.degenerate: For an empty open domain the only measure is the zero measure; an empty compact test set also contributes0. The nonempty compact approximation steps apply only when there is a set to approximate.
lem-ip-distributional-radon-representati.nonempty-choice: The approximation uses finite compact covers and the stated coded/local choices; it does not choose a test function independently at every point of an uncountable set.
lem-ip-distributional-radon-representati.iff-forward: NA: The asserted implication is uniqueness from agreement on test integrals. It is not an existence characterization of arbitrary distributions by Radon measures.
lem-ip-distributional-radon-representati.iff-reverse: NA: Equal measures of course have equal test integrals by definition, but no additional inverse representation theorem is claimed here. This item proves only the needed uniqueness implication.

lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjug.empty: The local crossing has actual over- and under-arcs in a nonempty link diagram. A crossing-free diagram simply has no such local relation; it is not a degenerate input crossing.
lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjug.one: The same global under-arc label may occur on both local under-sides of a crossing. The local conjugacy relation still uses the two oriented occurrences and does not require three distinct global generators.
lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjug.endpoints: The local under-arc endpoints on the crossing-ball boundary are joined with the prescribed basing paths. Their orientation and positive meridian convention determine which side is conjugated.
lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjug.degenerate: The crossing model has transverse branches and h>r>0; tangent branches and an unrecorded triple point are excluded. Basing changes are accounted for by the stated conjugations rather than ignored.
lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjug.nonempty-choice: The crossing chart, meridians and finitely many basing paths are supplied. No global choice of a path for every possible crossing diagram is part of the lemma.
lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjug.iff-forward: The Statement includes the genuine algebraic equivalence between the conjugacy equation and its relator. In proof3.1, multiplying m_t=m_o^{-1}m_s m_o on the right by m_t^{-1} gives the relator equal1.
lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjug.iff-reverse: Conversely the displayed relator m_o^{-1}m_s m_o m_t^{-1}=1 multiplied on the right by m_t recovers the conjugacy equation. This algebraic iff is distinct from the first paragraph orientation convention.

thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary.empty: A profile in the positively separated alternative is nonzero, so its finite active set cannot be empty. Empty-product conventions alone would not provide a valid alternative for these testing bounds.
thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary.zero: The limit u→0 is explicitly an impossibility regime, giving total risk tending1 and the fixed-level bound tending1−alpha. Exact zero noise remains excluded by epsilon>0.
thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary.one: One active coordinate is allowed in this nonsharp boundary theorem. Unlike the sharp Gaussian approximation, it requires no maximal-weight→0 condition.
thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary.endpoints: The two limiting regimes are u→0 and u→infinity through admissible positive profiles. Alpha stays in (0,1); their risk conclusions are not assertions involving an infinite normal quantile.
thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary.nonempty-choice: Countable Choice is retained for the sequence experiment. A specified admissible extremal/profile construction supplies the normalization, rather than an arbitrary selection of a minimizer.
thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary.iff-forward: NA: The theorem supplies limiting impossibility and consistency implications in two regimes. It is not an iff classification of every sequence with intermediate or oscillating u.
thm-ip-ellipsoid-detection-boundary.iff-reverse: NA: A limiting risk by itself is not claimed to force a unique profile or normalization regime. The two sufficient regimes do not establish such converses.

def-ip-frame-complement-property.zero: Zero measurement vectors are allowed but contribute nothing to either span. For m=0 both spans are {0}, so the complement property fails because d>=1.
def-ip-frame-complement-property.one: With one vector the complement property holds only in dimension1 when that vector is nonzero. In higher dimension a sole vector cannot span R^d on the nonempty side.
def-ip-frame-complement-property.endpoints: The partitions S=empty and S=all indices are included in the universal quantifier. They require the full frame to span since the empty side spans only {0}.
def-ip-frame-complement-property.nonempty-choice: The frame is finite and given, and the condition ranges over its finitely many subsets. No arbitrary selection from an indexed collection of vector spaces is made.
def-ip-frame-complement-property.iff-forward: NA: This Definition names a spanning condition on every partition. It does not itself prove the separate phase-retrieval implication from that condition.
def-ip-frame-complement-property.iff-reverse: NA: Recoverability from intensities is not used as a defining converse here; the separate real phase-retrieval theorem supplies that equivalence.

def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-wind.empty: The pattern and companion are actual embedded oriented circles. A winding-zero pattern is nonempty; it must not be confused with an empty pattern.
def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-wind.endpoints: The product-parallel convention names the inner and outer boundary tori and their meridian/longitude markings. An unmarked homeomorphism of abstract tori alone is not the specified peripheral identification.
def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-wind.degenerate: Winding number0 is allowed, including Whitehead-type patterns. The Definition does not assert incompressibility or essentiality of every companion torus without additional hypotheses.
def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-wind.nonempty-choice: The embedding of the solid torus and its prescribed peripheral identification are data. The item does not construct a canonical satellite for an arbitrary unmarked pair without such choices.
def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-wind.iff-forward: NA: Winding number and product-parallel terminology are definitions of supplied pattern data, not an iff theorem classifying satellites by their winding numbers.
def-satellite-pattern-companion-and-wind.iff-reverse: NA: A numerical winding value is not claimed sufficient to recover the pattern or companion, nor does it by itself force an essential companion torus.

lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seife.empty: At genus0 the symplectic basis is empty and the Arf basis sum is0. The underlying vector space still has its zero element, so its Gauss sum has one term equal1, not an empty sum.
lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seife.zero: At genus0 q(0)=0 on the zero vector space, the Arf sum is0 and the Gauss sum is1=2^0. A zero vector contributes the term (+1), while a zero-dimensional symplectic basis has no pairs.
lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seife.endpoints: There is no interval parameter in this Arf invariant statement. The relevant boundary is stabilization by either elementary Seifert enlargement, for which the hyperbolic added pair is explicitly handled.
lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seife.degenerate: The mod2 intersection pairing is symplectic, including the nondegenerate zero-dimensional case. A singular alternating form of positive dimension is not an admissible Seifert-intersection replacement.
lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seife.nonempty-choice: A finite symplectic basis is used under the stated algebraic framework; basis independence is proved by the Gauss-sum calculation. No infinite simultaneous selection of bases is needed.
lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seife.iff-forward: NA: The lemma constructs a basis-independent quadratic enhancement and Arf invariant. It does not assert that Arf0 is sufficient for sliceness.
lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seife.iff-reverse: NA: No classification of knots or Seifert forms by their Arf values is claimed. Stability of the invariant under the listed moves is not a converse classification.

lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-se.empty: The original surface and its capping disk have a nonempty common knot boundary. At genus0 the handle data may be empty, but the capped sphere and the resulting bounding three-manifold are not omitted.
lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-se.zero: For genus0 the resulting compact three-manifold has sphere boundary; the conclusion does not strengthen this to a three-ball. An empty Seifert matrix causes no obstruction to the stated hypersurface existence.
lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-se.one: There is one prescribed capping disk and one boundary knot. The construction does not need a second disjoint cap or assume all caps determine the same hypersurface.
lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-se.degenerate: The capping disk is locally flat and the hypersurface is two-sided with the prescribed positive product side. A merely continuous singular cap is outside the stated TOP hypothesis.
lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-se.iff-forward: NA: The implication constructs a Seifert hypersurface from a supplied locally flat cap. It does not characterize arbitrary embedded three-manifolds as coming from slice surfaces.
lem-locally-flat-slice-surface-bounds-se.iff-reverse: NA: No converse sliceness theorem follows from the abstract existence of a three-manifold with that boundary. The actual embedding and marked product side are retained inputs/conclusions.

lem-seifert-matrix-s-enlargement-preserv.zero: The starting genus may be0 and the coupling vectors or scalar z may vanish. The enlarged skew form still has its explicit unimodular hyperbolic block; zero coupling does not invalidate it.
lem-seifert-matrix-s-enlargement-preserv.one: One elementary enlargement adds a two-dimensional Seifert block. The finite metabolizer calculation covers either listed enlargement type, not an inadmissible one-dimensional Seifert form.
lem-seifert-matrix-s-enlargement-preserv.endpoints: The stabilization moves are the two explicitly displayed integral block forms. There is no continuous parameter endpoint or assertion about an arbitrary enlargement outside those forms.
lem-seifert-matrix-s-enlargement-preserv.degenerate: The algebraic concordance calculation permits singular V and zero couplings while retaining unimodularity of V−V^T. It does not assume V itself is invertible.
lem-seifert-matrix-s-enlargement-preserv.iff-forward: NA: The lemma proves that an elementary S-enlargement preserves algebraic concordance class. It does not identify every algebraic concordance with an S-equivalence.
lem-seifert-matrix-s-enlargement-preserv.iff-reverse: NA: Algebraic concordance of two forms is not claimed sufficient to connect them by the displayed enlargement moves. Only preservation under an actual given move is established.

cex-knot-kt-37-boundary-case.empty: The zero-crossing unknot has a cube with one vertex and its actual Frobenius module; it is not an empty chain complex. Empty-crossing data therefore already supply a nonzero raw value.
cex-knot-kt-37-boundary-case.endpoints: The positive and negative curls are the two Reidemeister-I orientations in the example. Formal q-gradings are compared as Laurent polynomials, with no root specialization that could hide the discrepancy.
cex-knot-kt-37-boundary-case.degenerate: The raw Euler values differ by the explicit grading/shift factors. A vanishing Euler characteristic at a special numerical q is not used as a substitute for the Laurent-polynomial counterexample.
cex-knot-kt-37-boundary-case.iff-forward: NA: A specific curl shows failure of the unnormalized invariant. The item does not assert an iff criterion identifying all possible Reidemeister-invariant normalizations.
cex-knot-kt-37-boundary-case.iff-reverse: NA: Agreement of one raw value with the unknot is not asserted sufficient for knot isotopy. The counterexample only refutes raw diagram invariance.

def-ribbon-disk-and-ribbon-knot.empty: The finite double-arc family may have m=0. An embedded disk in S3 is a ribbon immersion with no singularities, giving the unknot; the disk and its boundary knot are still nonempty.
